name: Zephaniah
overview: Zephaniah was a male Aaronic priest from the tribe of Levi, serving as the second-in-charge priest. His notable role in Scripture includes his position of authority within the priesthood. He was ultimately killed by the king of Babylon, marking a significant moment in his life and ministry.
namesAndTitles: The name Zephaniah means 'YHWH has hidden [to shelter]' or 'YHWH has hidden [as a treasure],' reflecting a divine aspect embedded in his identity. This meaning highlights a connection to God's protective or preserving care.
familyAndRelationships: Zephaniah is identified as a descendant of Aaron, the first high priest, which situates him within the priestly lineage. Beyond this, Scripture does not record additional family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Zephaniah's significance lies in his high-ranking priestly role during a turbulent period in Israel's history. As the second-in-charge priest, he held considerable responsibility in maintaining the spiritual leadership of the nation. His death at the hands of the Babylonian king underscores the severity of the Babylonian conquest and its impact on Israel's religious leadership.
